headings: Incyte's Approach to Drug Discovery and Development
Patents, Other Intellectual Property, and Product Exclusivity
paragraphs: Incyte is a global biopharmaceutical company engaged in the discovery, development and commercialization of proprietary therapeutics. Our global headquarters is located in Wilmington, Delaware, where we conduct discovery, clinical development and commercial operations. We also conduct clinical development and commercial operations from our European headquarters in Morges, Switzerland, and our other offices across Europe, as well as our Japanese headquarters in Tokyo and our Canadian headquarters in Montreal.

We are focused in three therapeutic areas that are defined by the indications of our approved medicines and the diseases for which our clinical candidates are being developed. These therapeutic areas are: Hematology, Oncology, and Inflammation and Autoimmunity ("IAI").

Our hematology franchise includes four approved products, JAKAFI (ruxolitinib), ICLUSIG (ponatinib), MONJUVI (tafasitamab-cxix)/MINJUVI (tafasitamab) and NIKTIMVO (axatilimab-csfr), as well as multiple clinical development programs.

JAKAFI (ruxolitinib) was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") in November 2011 for the treatment of adults with intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis ("MF"); in December 2014 for the treatment of adults with polycythemia vera ("PV") who have had an inadequate response to or are intolerant of hydroxyurea; in May 2019 for the treatment of steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease ("GVHD") in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older; and in September 2021 for the treatment of chronic GVHD after failure of one or two lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older. MF and PV are both myeloproliferative neoplasms ("MPNs"), a group of rare blood cancers, and GVHD is an adverse immune response to an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant ("HSCT").

The FDA has granted JAKAFI orphan drug status for MF, PV and GVHD. In addition, ruxolitinib phosphate qualifies for the Small Biotech Exception from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services ("CMS") under the Inflation Reduction Act.

Myelofibrosis. MF, a rare, life-threatening condition, is considered the most serious of the MPNs and can occur either as primary MF or as secondary MF in patients who previously had PV or essential thrombocythemia ("ET"). In November 2011, the FDA approved JAKAFI for the treatment of adults with intermediate or high-risk MF, including primary MF, post-PV MF and post-ET MF. There were no FDA approved therapies for MF until the approval of JAKAFI.

Polycythemia Vera. PV is an MPN typically characterized by elevated hematocrit, the volume percentage of red blood cells in whole blood, which can lead to a thickening of the blood and an increased risk of blood clots, as well as an elevated white blood cell and platelet count. In December 2014, the FDA approved JAKAFI for the treatment of patients with PV who have had an inadequate response to or are intolerant of hydroxyurea.

Graft-versus-host disease. GVHD is a condition that can occur after an allogeneic HSCT (the transfer of genetically dissimilar stem cells or tissue) where the donated bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cells view the recipient's body as foreign and attack various tissues. In May 2019, the FDA approved JAKAFI for the treatment of steroid-refractory acute GVHD in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older. In September 2021, the FDA approved JAKAFI for the treatment of chronic GVHD after failure of one or two lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older.

Under our collaboration agreement with Novartis Pharmaceutical International Ltd. ("Novartis"), Novartis received exclusive development and commercialization rights to ruxolitinib outside of the United States for all hematologic and oncologic indications and sells ruxolitinib outside of the United States under the name JAKAVI. We are eligible to receive development and sales milestones as well as royalties from product sales outside the United States.

We have retained all development and commercialization rights to JAKAFI in the United States. We market JAKAFI in the United States through our own specialty sales force and commercial team. JAKAFI is distributed primarily through a network of specialty pharmacy providers and wholesalers that allow for efficient delivery of the medication by mail directly to patients or direct delivery to the patient's pharmacy.
We hold patents that cover the composition of matter and use of ruxolitinib and its salt. These patents, including applicable extensions, currently expire in mid and late 2028, respectively.

In June 2016, we acquired the European operations of ARIAD Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and obtained an exclusive license to develop and commercialize ICLUSIG (ponatinib), a kinase inhibitor, in Europe and other select countries. The primary target for ICLUSIG is BCR-ABL, an abnormal tyrosine kinase that is expressed in chronic myeloid leukemia ("CML") and Philadelphia-chromosome positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia ("Ph+ ALL").

In the European Union, ICLUSIG is approved for the treatment of adult patients with chronic phase, accelerated phase or blast phase CML who are resistant to dasatinib or nilotinib; who are intolerant to dasatinib or nilotinib and for whom subsequent treatment with imatinib is not clinically appropriate; or who have the T315I mutation. In the European Union, ICLUSIG also is approved for the treatment of adult patients with Ph+ ALL who are resistant to dasatinib; who are intolerant to dasatinib and for whom subsequent treatment with imatinib is not clinically appropriate; or who have the T315I mutation.

In January 2020, we and MorphoSys AG ("MorphoSys") entered into a collaboration and license agreement to further develop and commercialize MorphoSys' proprietary anti-CD19 antibody tafasitamab (formerly MOR208) globally. In February 2024, we entered into a purchase agreement with MorphoSys relating to tafasitamab. As a result, we now hold exclusive global rights for tafasitamab, and the collaboration and license agreement was terminated.

headings: If we fail to comply with applicable laws and regulations, we could lose our approval to market our products or be subject to other governmental enforcement activity.

The testing, manufacturing, marketing and sale of our products could expose us to product liability and other risks. Side effects and other problems experienced by patients from the use of our products could:
If we market our products in a manner that violates various laws and regulations, we may be subject to civil or criminal penalties.
Competition for our products could harm our business and result in a decrease in our revenue.
We may be unsuccessful in our efforts to discover and develop drug candidates and commercialize drug products.
Changes in government pricing policies, including the enactment of "most favored nation" pricing legislation, could adversely affect our business.
paragraphs: We depend heavily on our lead product, JAKAFI (ruxolitinib), which is marketed as JAKAVI outside the United States. If we are unable to maintain revenues from JAKAFI or those revenues decrease, our business may be materially harmed.

JAKAFI is the first product marketed by us to be approved for sale in the United States. While we also sell our and our licensors' other approved products ICLUSIG, PEMAZYRE, MONJUVI/MINJUVI, OPZELURA, ZYNYZ and NIKTIMVO and our exclusive licensees sell OLUMIANT and TABRECTA, we anticipate that JAKAFI product sales will continue to contribute a significant percentage of our total revenues over the next several years. However, we expect that JAKAFI product sales will begin to decline upon the expiration of our patent exclusivity in 2028.
The continued commercial success of JAKAFI and our ability to maintain and continue to increase revenues from the sale of JAKAFI will depend on a number of factors, including:

•the number of patients diagnosed with intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, uncontrolled polycythemia vera or steroid-refractory graft-versus-host disease and the number of such patients that may be treated with JAKAFI;
•the acceptance of JAKAFI by patients and the healthcare community;

•whether physicians, patients and healthcare payors view JAKAFI as therapeutically effective and safe relative to cost and any alternative therapies, as well as whether patients will continue to use JAKAFI;

headings: License Agreements, Business Relationships and Acquisitions
Critical Accounting Policies and Significant Estimates
paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes included elsewhere in this report.

A discussion of our financial performance for the year ended December 31, 2025 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024 appears below under the captions "Results of Operations" and "Liquidity and Capital Resources." A discussion of our financial performance for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023 can be found under the same captions in Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 10, 2025, which is available free of charge on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov and our Investor Relations website at investor.incyte.com/financials/annual-reports. These website addresses are intended to be inactive, textual references only. None of the materials on, or accessible through, these websites are part of this report or are incorporated by reference herein.

Incyte is a global biopharmaceutical company engaged in the discovery, development and commercialization of proprietary therapeutics. Our global headquarters is located in Wilmington, Delaware, where we conduct discovery, clinical development and commercial operations. We also conduct clinical development and commercial operations from our European headquarters in Morges, Switzerland, and our other offices across Europe, as well as our Japanese headquarters in Tokyo and our Canadian headquarters in Montreal.

We are focused in three therapeutic areas that are defined by the indications of our approved medicines and the diseases for which our clinical candidates are being developed. These therapeutic areas are: Hematology, Oncology, and Inflammation and Autoimmunity ("IAI"). We are also eligible to receive milestones and royalties on molecules discovered by us and licensed to third parties.

Our portfolio focuses on areas of high unmet medical need and includes compounds in various stages, ranging from preclinical to late-stage development and commercialized products. Our approved products are JAKAFI (ruxolitinib), ICLUSIG (ponatinib), PEMAZYRE (pemigatinib), OPZELURA (ruxolitinib cream), MINJUVI (tafasitamab), MONJUVI (tafasitamab-cxix) and ZYNYZ (retifanlimab-dlwr), as well as NIKTIMVO (axatilimab-csfr) which is co-commercialized.

Our revenues depend on continued sales of our products, and we depend substantially on product revenues from JAKAFI. We must develop and commercialize new products to achieve revenue growth and to offset revenue losses from the loss of product exclusivity of JAKAFI in 2028 and the launch of competing products. For additional information, including information on the expirations of patents for various products, see Part I, Item 1 of this report, under the headings "Business—Patents, Other Intellectual Property, and Product Exclusivity" and "Business—Competition." We devote substantial resources to research and development activities and to acquire rights to new product candidates and technologies, but successful product development in the biopharmaceutical industry is highly uncertain.

Our product revenues also face challenges from economic conditions and drug pricing initiatives driven by governments and private payors. See Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors" of this report for a further discussion of certain factors that could impact our future product revenues.

We establish business relationships, including collaborative arrangements with other companies and medical research institutions, to assist in the clinical development and/or commercialization of certain of our drugs and drug candidates and to provide support for our research programs. We also evaluate opportunities for acquiring products or rights to products and technologies that are complementary to our business from other companies and medical research institutions.

The preparation of financial statements requires us to make estimates, assumptions and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities. On an ongoing basis, we evaluate our estimates. We base our estimates on historical experience and various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form our basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources. Actual results may differ from those estimates under different assumptions or conditions. We believe the following critical accounting policies reflect the more significant judgments and estimates used in the preparation of the consolidated financial statements. See Note 1 of Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for a complete list of our significant accounting policies.

Revenue Recognition. We recognize revenue only when we have satisfied a performance obligation through transferring control of the promised good or service to a customer in an amount that reflects the consideration we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services. We apply the following five-step model in order to determine this amount: (i) identification of the promised goods or services in the contract; (ii) determination of whether the promised goods or services are performance obligations, including whether they are distinct in the context of the contract; (iii) measurement of the transaction price, including the constraint on variable consideration; (iv) allocation of the transaction price to the performance obligations; and (v) recognition of revenue when (or as) the Company satisfies each performance obligation, which for the Company is at a point in time. We also assess collectability based primarily on the customer's payment history and on the creditworthiness of the customer.

Product revenues are recognized once we satisfy the performance obligation at a point in time under the revenue recognition criteria as described above. We recognize revenues for product received by our customers net of allowances for customer credits, including estimated rebates, chargebacks, discounts, returns, distribution service fees, patient assistance programs, and government rebates, such as the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program and Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage reimbursements in the United States and mandated discounts in Europe. These sales allowances and accruals are recorded based on estimates which are described in detail below. Estimates are assessed as of the end of each reporting period and are updated to reflect current information. We believe that our sales allowances and accruals are reasonable and appropriate based on current facts and circumstances. As of December 31, 2025, a 5% change in our sales allowance and accruals would have had an approximate $103.8 million impact on our income before taxes.

Customer Credits: Our customers are offered various forms of consideration, including allowances, service fees and prompt payment discounts. We expect our customers will earn prompt payment discounts and, therefore, we deduct the full amount of these discounts from total product sales when revenues are recognized. Service fees are also deducted from total product sales as they are earned.

Rebates and Discounts: We accrue rebates for mandated discounts under the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program in the United States and mandated discounts in Europe in markets where government-sponsored healthcare systems are the primary payors for healthcare. These accruals are based on statutory discount rates and expected utilization as well as historical data we have accumulated since product launch.

Our estimates for expected utilization of commercial insurance rebates are based on data received from our customers. Rebates are generally invoiced and paid in arrears so that the accrual balance consists of an estimate of the amount expected to be incurred for the current quarter's activity, plus an accrual balance for known prior quarters' unpaid rebates. If actual future rebates vary from estimates, we may need to adjust prior period accruals, which would affect revenue in the period of adjustment.

headings: Incyte 的藥物發現與開發方法
專利、其他智慧財產權及產品獨佔權
paragraphs: Incyte 是一家全球性生物製藥公司，從事專利藥物的發現、開發與商業化。本公司全球總部位於美國特拉華州威明頓市，我們在此進行發現、臨牀開發與商業運作。我們也在瑞士莫熱斯的歐洲總部進行臨牀開發與商業運作，並在歐洲其他辦事處，以及日本東京的日本總部與加拿大蒙特利爾的加拿大總部進行相關業務。
我們專注於三個治療領域，這些領域由本公司已核准藥物的適應症以及臨牀候選藥物正在開發的疾病所定義。這些治療領域為：血液學、腫瘤學，以及發炎與自身免疫（"IAI"）。
本公司血液學產品線包括四種已核准的產品，JAKAFI（ruxolitinib）、ICLUSIG（ponatinib）、MONJUVI（tafasitamab-cxix）/MINJUVI（tafasitamab）以及NIKTIMVO（axatilimab-csfr），以及多個臨牀開發計畫。

JAKAFI（ruxolitinib）於2011年11月獲美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，用於治療中度或高風險骨髓纖維化（"MF"）的成人患者；於2014年12月核准，用於治療對氫氧化尿素反應不足或無法耐受的成人患者之癲癇紅血球增多症（"PV"）；於2019年5月核准，用於治療12歲以上成人及兒童患者的急性移植物抗宿主疾病（"GVHD"）；於2021年9月核准，用於治療在系統性治療失敗後的慢性GVHD，適用於12歲以上成人及兒童患者。MF與PV皆為骨髓增殖性腫瘤（"MPNs"），是一羣罕見的血液癌症，而GVHD為對異體造血幹細胞移植（"HSCT"）的不良免疫反應。
美國食品藥物管理局已授予JAKAFI針對MF、PV及GVHD的罕見疾病藥物地位。此外，ruxolitinib磷酸鹽符合美國醫療保險與醫療補助服務中心（"CMS"）根據《通脹減稅法案》對小型生物技術公司的豁免條款。
骨髓纖維化。MF是一種罕見且危及生命的疾病，被視為MPNs中最嚴重的類型，可發生於原發性MF或次發性MF，即先前患有PV或原發性血小板增多症（"ET"）的患者。2011年11月，美國食品藥物管理局核准JAKAFI用於治療中度或高風險MF的成人患者，包括原發性MF、PV後MF及ET後MF。在JAKAFI核准之前，尚無FDA核准的MF治療方式。
癲癇紅血球增多症。PV為一種MPN，通常特徵為紅血球壓積升高，即全血中紅血球體積百分比，可能導致血液變稠，增加血栓風險，以及白血球與血小板計數升高。2014年12月，美國食品藥物管理局核准JAKAFI用於治療對氫氧化尿素反應不足或無法耐受的PV患者。

移植物抗宿主疾病。GVHD為一種在異體HSCT（遺傳上不相似的幹細胞或組織的轉移）後可能發生的疾病，其中捐贈的骨髓或外周血幹細胞將受體的身體視為異物並攻擊各類組織。2019年5月，美國食品藥物管理局核准JAKAFI用於治療12歲以上成人及兒童患者的急性GVHD，對類固醇治療無效。2021年9月，美國食品藥物管理局核准JAKAFI用於治療在系統性治療失敗後的慢性GVHD，適用於12歲以上成人及兒童患者。
根據我們與 Novartis Pharmaceutical International Ltd. ("Novartis") 籤訂的合作協議，Novartis 取得 ruxolitinib 在美國以外地區就所有血液學及腫瘤學適應症的獨家開發與商業化權利，並在美國以外地區以 JAKAVI 名稱銷售 ruxolitinib。我們有資格取得開發與銷售里程碑款項以及來自美國以外地區產品銷售的版稅。
我們保留了 JAKAFI 在美國的開發與商業化權利。我們透過自己的專門銷售團隊及商業團隊在美國市場推廣 JAKAFI。JAKAFI 主要透過專門藥房供應商及經銷商網路分銷，以利透過郵遞方式直接送達患者或直接送達患者藥房。
我們持有涵蓋 ruxolitinib 及其鹽類組成物質與用途的專利。這些專利，包括適用的延長期限，目前分別於 2028 年中至晚期到期。
2016 年 6 月，我們取得 ARIAD Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 的歐洲業務，並取得在歐洲及其他特定國家開發與商業化 ICLUSIG (ponatinib)，一種絲氨酸/蘇氨酸蛋白激酶抑制劑的獨家許可。ICULISG 的主要目標為 BCR-ABL，一種在慢性髓細胞白血病 ("CML") 及費城染色體陽性急性淋巴細胞白血病 ("Ph+ ALL") 中異常表現的酪胺酸激酶。

在歐盟，ICULISG 已核准用於治療對 dasatinib 或 nilotinib 抵抗的成人慢性期、加速期或 blast 期 CML 患者；對 dasatinib 或 nilotinib 不耐受且隨後使用 imatinib 不 clinically appropriate 的患者；或具有 T315I 突變的患者。在歐盟，ICULISG 也已核准用於治療對 dasatinib 抵抗的成人 Ph+ ALL 患者；對 dasatinib 不耐受且隨後使用 imatinib 不 clinically appropriate 的患者；或具有 T315I 突變的患者。

2020 年 1 月，我們與 MorphoSys AG ("MorphoSys") 籤訂合作與許可協議，以進一步開發與商業化 MorphoSys 的專利抗 CD19 抗體 tafasitamab (原為 MOR208) 全球。2024 年 2 月，我們與 MorphoSys 籤訂買賣協議，與 tafasitamab 相關。因此，我們現持有 tafasitamab 的全球獨家權利，且合作與許可協議已終止。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本報告中其他處所載的合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。

有關我們2025年12月31日財年與2024年12月31日財年財務表現的討論，請參閱本報告中標題為『營運成果』及『流動性及資本資源』的部分。有關我們2024年12月31日財年與2023年12月31日財年財務表現的討論，請參閱我們2024年12月31日財年10-K年度報告中相同標題的部分，該報告於2025年2月10日提交至證券交易委員會（SEC），並可在SEC網站www.sec.gov及我們投資者關係網站investor.incyte.com/financials/annual-reports免費取得。這些網站地址僅為靜態文字參考，並非活躍連結。這些網站上或透過這些網站存取的資料並非本報告的一部分，亦未經參考引述 herein。
Incyte為一全球性生物製藥公司，專注於自有專利治療藥物的發現、開發與商業化。我們的全球總部位於特拉華州威明頓市，我們在該地進行發現、臨牀開發與商業運作。我們也在瑞士莫爾日的歐洲總部進行臨牀開發與商業運作，並在歐洲其他辦公室，以及日本東京的日本總部與加拿大蒙特利爾的加拿大總部進行相關運作。
我們專注於三個治療領域，這些領域由我們核准藥物的適應症及我們臨牀候選藥物正在開發的疾病所定義。這些治療領域為：血液學、腫瘤學，以及發炎與自身免疫（"IAI"）。我們也有資格從我們發現並授權給第三方的分子獲得里程碑付款與版稅。

我們的產品組合專注於高未滿足醫療需求的領域，包含處於不同階段的化合物，從臨牀前到晚期開發，以及已商業化產品。我們核准的產品包括JAKAFI（ruxolitinib）、ICLUSIG（ponatinib）、PEMAZYRE（pemigatinib）、OPZELURA（ruxolitinib乳霜）、MINJUVI（tafasitamab）、MONJUVI（tafasitamab-cxix）與ZYNYZ（retifanlimab-dlwr），以及與他人共同商業化的NIKTIMVO（axatilimab-csfr）。

我們的收入依賴於產品持續銷售，我們 substantially 依賴JAKAFI的產品收入。我們必須開發與商業化新產品以實現收入成長，並抵銷JAKAFI在2028年失去產品專屬權及競爭產品上市所造成的收入減損。有關更多資訊，包括各產品專利到期資訊，請參閱本報告第一部分，項目1，標題為『業務—專利、其他智慧財產權及產品專屬權』及『業務—競爭』的部分。我們投入大量資源於研究與開發活動，以及取得新產品候選藥物與技術的權利，但生物製藥產業中成功的產品開發極為不確定。
我們的產品收入也面臨經濟條件及政府與私人支付者推動的藥物價格管制等挑戰。有關可能影響我們未來產品收入的某些因素的進一步討論，請參閱本報告第一部分，項目1A，『風險因素』。
我們建立商業關係，包括與其他公司及醫療研究機構的合作安排，以協助我們某些藥物及藥物候選藥物的臨牀開發與/或商業化，並提供我們研究計畫的支持。我們也評估從其他公司及醫療研究機構取得與我們業務補充的產品或技術的機會。

財務報表的編製需要我們做出估計、假設與判斷，這些會影響資產、負債、收入與費用的報導數額，以及相關的或有資產與負債揭露。我們持續評估這些估計數值。我們的估計數值是基於歷史經驗與我們認為在特定情況下合理的其他假設，這些結果成為我們判斷非易於從其他來源取得的資產與負債之帳面價值的基礎。實際結果可能因不同的假設或條件而與這些估計數值不同。我們認為下列關鍵會計政策反映了我們在編製合併財務報表時所使用的較重要判斷與估計。請參閱合併財務報表附註第 1 項，以取得我們重要會計政策的完整清單。

收入認列。我們僅在滿足客戶的績效義務，即將承諾的商品或服務的控制權轉移給客戶，且金額反映我們預期會因這些商品或服務而收到的對價時，才認列收入。我們依照以下五步驟模型來確定此金額：(i) 識別合約中的承諾商品或服務；(ii) 判斷這些承諾商品或服務是否為績效義務，包括它們在合約情境下是否為獨立的；(iii) 測量交易金額，包括變動對價的限制；(iv) 將交易金額分配至績效義務；以及 (v) 在 (或隨著) 本公司滿足每一績效義務時認列收入，對本公司而言，此時點為績效義務的履行時點。我們也主要根據客戶的付款紀錄與客戶的信用狀況來評估其償還能力。

產品收入是在我們滿足績效義務，即在收入認列標準所描述的時點，認列產品收入。我們在認列收入時，會針對客戶所取得的產品，扣除客戶信用額度、包括預估的折扣、退貨、分銷服務費用、病人協助計畫與政府折扣，例如美國的醫療保險藥物折扣計畫與 Medicare Part D 計畫藥物覆蓋補償，以及歐洲的強制折扣。這些銷售信用與應計數值是根據下列詳細說明的估計數值進行記錄。估計數值在每個會計期間結算時評估，並根據最新資訊進行更新。我們認為，根據目前的實際情況，我們的銷售信用與應計數值是合理且適當的。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的銷售信用與應計數值變動 5%，將對我們的所得稅前淨利產生約 103.8 億美元的影響。
客戶信用：我們的客戶會獲得各種形式的對價，包括信用額度、服務費用與即時付款折扣。我們預期客戶將獲得即時付款折扣，因此在認列收入時，我們會從總產品銷售額中扣除這些折扣的全部金額。服務費用也會從總產品銷售額中扣除，因為這些費用已經產生。
折扣與回扣：我們根據美國的醫療保險藥物回扣計畫與歐洲的強制折扣，在政府主導的醫療系統為主要支付方的市場，為強制折扣進行回扣應計。這些應計數值是根據法定折扣率與預期使用率，以及我們自產品上市以來累積的歷史資料進行計算。
我們對商業保險回扣預期使用率的估計數值是根據我們客戶提供的資料。回扣通常是在事後開票與付款，因此應計餘額包含當前季度活動預期產生的金額，加上已知之前季度未付款回扣的應計餘額。如果未來實際回扣與估計數值不同，我們可能需要調整前一會計期間的應計數值，這將影響調整期間的收入。

headings: 若我們未能遵守適用之法律及法規，我們可能喪失核准上市銷售產品之許可，或面臨其他政府執法行動。
我們產品之測試、製造、行銷及銷售可能使我們面臨產品責任及其他風險。患者因使用我們產品而遭遇之副作用及其他問題可能：
若我們以違反各項法律及法規之方式行銷產品，我們可能面臨民事或刑事處罰。
我們產品之競爭可能損害我們業務，並導致我們營業收入減少。
我們可能無法成功進行藥物候選品之發現與開發，並實現藥物產品之商業化。
政府價格政策之變更，包括 enactment of "most favored nation" 價格立法，可能對我們業務產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 我們高度依賴我們的主力產品 JAKAFI (ruxolitinib)，該產品在美國以外地區以 JAKAVI 名稱行銷。若我們無法維持 JAKAFI 的營收或該營收減少，將可能對本公司業務造成重大損害。

JAKAFI 是本公司首個在美國獲准銷售的產品。雖然我們也銷售本公司及授權公司的其他核准產品 ICLUSIG、PEMAZYRE、MONJUVI/MINJUVI、OPZELURA、ZYNYZ 和 NIKTIMVO，且本公司獨家授權的授權方銷售 OLUMIANT 和 TABRECTA，但我們預期 JAKAFI 的產品銷售將在未來幾年繼續佔據本公司總營收的重要比例。然而，我們預期 JAKAFI 的產品銷售將在 2028 年專利獨佔權到期後開始下降。
JAKAFI 繼續商業成功以及本公司維持並持續提高 JAKAFI 銷售收入的能力，將取決於多項因素，包括：
•被診斷為中度或高風險骨髓纖維化、無法控制的癲癇性紅細胞增多症或類固醇難治性移植物抗宿主疾病之患者的數量，以及可能接受 JAKAFI 治療的患者數量；
•患者及醫療界對 JAKAFI 的接受度；
•醫師、患者及醫療給付者是否認為 JAKAFI 相對於成本及任何替代療法而言具有治療效果且安全，以及患者是否會持續使用 JAKAFI；
